(A) After smoothing its edges, Noor painted the wooden bookmark and left it to dry.
(B) She used the drawing as a guide to cut the shape.
(C) Once the shape had been cut, she smoothed its edges.
(D) Noor first drew a design for a wooden bookmark.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

Match each word in List-I with its meaning in List-II. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) "reluctant"
(B) "assertive"
(C) "discreet"
(D) "transient"

List-II
(I) careful in what you say or do, in order to keep something secret
(II) hesitating before doing something because you do not want to do it
(III) continuing for only a short time
(IV) expressing opinions or desires strongly and with confidence, so that people take notice

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The correct matches are "reluctant" with (II), "assertive" with (IV), "discreet" with (I), and "transient" with (III). Option B gives all four matches; the other options mismatch at least two words and meanings.

body: Two reviewers considered an explanation for a late delivery. One found its wording ambiguous, and another remained sceptical; the lead reviewer called it plausible. Which phrase gives the closest meaning of "plausible" as used here?
options: ["Reasonable and likely to be true","Capable of being understood in more than one way","Happening only occasionally or at irregular intervals","Having doubts that a claim or statement is true"]
explanation: For an excuse or explanation, "plausible" means reasonable and likely to be true. The other options give the meanings of ambiguous, sporadic and sceptical, respectively.

options: ["Requiring sustained effort and energy","Expecting a successful outcome","Showing little interest in the work","Being able to do many different things"]
explanation: The context shows Nila performing several different kinds of work, so "versatile" means being able to do many different things. The other options refer to sustained effort, expectation of success and lack of interest, rather than a range of abilities.

Match each response in List-I with the description in List-II.

List-I
(A) Nila hesitates before joining a reading group because she does not want to join.
(B) Kabir hesitates before beginning revision because he is waiting for a quiet room, although he wants to begin.
(C) Sara begins a group task straightaway even though she does not want to do it.
(D) Imran begins revision straightaway because he wants to begin.

List-II
(I) Hesitates before doing the action because the person does not want to do it
(II) Hesitates before doing the action although the person wants to do it
(III) Does the action without hesitation although the person does not want to do it
(IV) Does the action without hesitation and wants to do it

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Nila matches (I), which gives the stated meaning of "reluctant": she hesitates because she does not want to join. Kabir matches (II), while Sara matches (III) and Imran matches (IV), according to whether each person hesitates and wants to do the action.

body: At a museum, Asha asked questions about exhibits in several unrelated sections. Dev completed the task for one display, declined the optional sections and said he did not want to learn about anything else there. Which word best describes Dev’s attitude as the opposite of Asha’s inquisitive attitude?
options: ["discreet","ambiguous","inevitable","uninterested"]
explanation: In the relevant sense, “inquisitive” means being very interested in learning about many different things. Dev’s stated lack of interest in learning about the other sections contrasts with Asha’s interest in several exhibits, so “uninterested” is the best antonym here.

body: The entry register records that the courier arrived after the office gate had closed. The courier explains that this is why the delivery was late, and the manager calls the explanation “plausible”. In this context, “plausible” is closest in meaning to:
options: ["sporadic","optimistic","credible","vigilant"]
explanation: A plausible explanation is reasonable and likely to be true, so “credible” is the closest meaning. “Sporadic” describes irregular occurrence, “optimistic” describes expecting good things, and “vigilant” describes being careful to notice danger or trouble.

body:
Match each situation with the part of the meaning of "arrogant" that it most directly illustrates.

List-I
(A) A person boasts about their own status but otherwise treats people considerately and courteously.
(B) A person speaks offensively but neither claims superiority nor disregards other people’s needs.
(C) A person makes a decision without considering its effect on others, but does not boast or speak offensively.
(D) A person boasts of being superior, speaks offensively and ignores other people’s concerns.

List-II
(I) Showing little thought for other people
(II) Behaving in a proud way
(III) Behaving in an unpleasant way
(IV) The complete meaning of "arrogant"

explanation: The meaning of "arrogant" includes proud behaviour, unpleasant behaviour and showing little thought for others. Situations (A), (B) and (C) each isolate one of those features, respectively; (D) combines all three.

body: The supplier predicted that its new system would halve a shop’s energy use. Mira asked for evidence before accepting the prediction and remained “sceptical”. Which word is closest in meaning to “sceptical” as used here?
options: ["doubtful","elated","frugal","gregarious"]
explanation: Mira asks for evidence before accepting the supplier’s prediction, showing that she doubts whether the claim is true. Therefore, “doubtful” is the closest synonym. “Elated” describes happiness and excitement, “frugal” describes using only what is necessary, and “gregarious” describes liking to be with other people.

Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
(A) After confirming the match, Ravi opened the parcel and counted the notebooks inside.
(B) Finally, he recorded the count on the receipt and placed the notebooks in the cupboard.
(C) Ravi received a sealed parcel addressed to his class.
(D) Before opening it, Ravi checked the address against the class's order receipt.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The coherent order is C-D-A-B: C introduces the parcel, D checks its address before it is opened, A follows the confirmed match and counts the notebooks, and B records that count and puts the notebooks away. This follows the events’ stated order.

body:
Match each situation in List-I with the adjective in List-II that best describes it. Each entry in List-I is to be matched with one entry in List-II, and each entry in List-II is to be used once.

List-I
(A) A journey that demands a lot of effort and energy over several days
(B) A person careful in speech to keep a private matter secret
(C) A speaker who expresses an opinion strongly and confidently so that people notice
(D) A donor who is kind, helpful and generous

List-II
(I) Benevolent
(II) Arduous
(III) Assertive
(IV) Discreet

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The journey’s sustained effort matches “arduous”, while protecting a private matter through careful speech matches “discreet”. The speaker is “assertive”, and the donor is “benevolent”; therefore, option D gives the correct mapping.

Which inference is best supported by Rohan’s response?
A. Asking another person to help can itself be a useful way to assist.
B. A person can assist only by carrying out the search personally.
C. An assigned task should be left unfinished whenever someone needs help.
D. Assistance is useful only after the person in need has solved the problem.

explanation: Rohan could not search while carrying the box, and the costumes were needed soon, so he took them to the hall and asked another volunteer to search. After the notebook was found, he realised that asking the right person could also be useful assistance.

Select the correct statement(s) about comparative statements and common size statements.

(A) Comparative statements express each financial-statement item as a percentage of a common item.
(B) Common size statements express each financial-statement item as a percentage of a common item.
(C) Common-size analysis is also known as horizontal analysis.
(D) Comparative-statement analysis is also known as vertical analysis.
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(A) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only","(B) only"]
explanation: Common size statements express each item as a percentage of a common item, so statement (B) is correct. Comparative analysis is horizontal analysis, while common-size analysis is vertical analysis; therefore, statements (A), (C) and (D) are incorrect.

To be more specific, the analysis is undertaken to serve the following purposes (objectives): • to assess the current profitability and operational efficiency of the firm as a whole as well as its different departments so as to judge the financial health of the firm. • to ascertain the relative importance of different components of the financial position of the firm. • to identify the reasons for change in the profitability/financial position of the firm. • to judge the ability of the firm to repay its debt and assessing the short-term as well as the long-term liquidity position of the firm. Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. body: On dissolution, a firm’s non-cash assets with an aggregate book value of ₹6,00,000 are sold for ₹4,80,000. External liabilities with an aggregate book value of ₹1,50,000 are settled in cash for ₹1,35,000, and realisation expenses of ₹15,000 are paid in cash. Partners A, B and C share profits and losses in the ratio 3:2:1. These are the only assets, liabilities and realisation transactions; no partner takes over an asset or liability, and there are no unrecorded items. What amount of the realisation loss is debited to B’s capital account?
explanation: The Realisation Account is debited by ₹6,00,000 for the assets, ₹1,35,000 for the liabilities paid and ₹15,000 for expenses, totalling ₹7,50,000. It is credited by ₹4,80,000 from asset sales and ₹1,50,000 for the liabilities transferred, totalling ₹6,30,000, so the realisation loss is ₹1,20,000. B’s share is 2/6 of that loss, or ₹40,000.

body: A company issues shares of nominal value ₹10 each at par. It has called up ₹8 per share to date. A shareholder pays ₹10 per share, and no amount due on the shares remains unpaid. How should the ₹2 per share paid beyond the amount called up be classified?
options: ["Calls in Advance, for which a separate account is maintained.","Calls in Arrears, for which a separate account is mandatory.","Securities Premium, credited to a separate reserve account.","Forfeiture of Shares, with the amount received credited to Forfeiture Shares Account."]
explanation: The shareholder has paid ₹2 per share more than the ₹8 called up. An amount paid in excess of the amount due is Calls in Advance, for which a separate account is maintained.
supporting_excerpts: [{"id":"ncert-leac201","locator":"pdf-page-66","text":"66 Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements Calls in Arrears: Sometimes, the full amount called on allotment and/or call (calls) is not received from the allottees/shareholders. The amount not so received are cumulatively called ‘Unpaid calls’ or ‘Calls in Arrears’. However, it is not mandatory for a company to maintain a separate Calls-in-Arrears Account. body: For a 365-day accounting period, a firm’s trade payables comprise only creditors and bills payable. At the beginning of the period, creditors were ₹70,000 and bills payable were ₹30,000. At the end, creditors were ₹90,000 and bills payable were ₹50,000. Net purchases for the period were ₹6,00,000; no separate credit-purchase figure is provided. Use the arithmetic mean of beginning and ending trade payables. What was the firm’s average payment period, rounded to the nearest whole day?
options: ["85 days","49 days","73 days","146 days"]
explanation: Average trade payables are (₹70,000 + ₹30,000 + ₹90,000 + ₹50,000) ÷ 2 = ₹1,20,000. The trade payables turnover ratio is ₹6,00,000 ÷ ₹1,20,000 = 5 times. Therefore, the average payment period is 365 ÷ 5 = 73 days.

body: A flood caused a non-recurring loss at Nira Ltd.; for this question, the flood event is treated as an extraordinary item. The company’s only cash outflows directly arising from the flood were ₹2,40,000 for disposal of flood-damaged inventory and site clean-up, ₹1,35,000 for emergency repairs, and ₹75,000 for temporary storage. It also received ₹90,000 insurance compensation for the same event and paid ₹50,000 for routine maintenance unrelated to the flood. What total gross cash outflow arising from the extraordinary event should be calculated for separate disclosure? Do not offset receipts or include unrelated payments.
explanation: The flood is treated as a non-recurring extraordinary event, and cash flows associated with extraordinary items are disclosed separately. The gross outflow is ₹2,40,000 + ₹1,35,000 + ₹75,000 = ₹4,50,000; the insurance compensation is a receipt, and the routine maintenance payment is unrelated under the stem.

body:
A company is reviewing a proposed buy-back of shares. Match each aspect of the buy-back in List-I with the corresponding requirement in List-II.

List-I
(A) Maximum buy-back amount in one financial year
(B) Debt-equity ratio after the buy-back
(C) Payment status of shares selected for buy-back
(D) Time allowed to complete the buy-back after passing a special resolution

List-II
(I) Completion within 12 months from the date of passing the special resolution
(II) Amount should not exceed 25% of paid-up capital and free reserves
(III) Ratio should not be more than 2:1
(IV) All shares bought back should be fully paid-up

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The annual buy-back amount should not exceed 25% of paid-up capital and free reserves, while the post-buy-back debt-equity ratio should not be more than 2:1. Shares bought back must be fully paid-up, and the buy-back must be completed within 12 months from the date of passing the special resolution; these requirements give the mapping in option D.

body:
A company presents its balance-sheet figures for two periods side by side. It used the same accounting principles in both periods. Consider the following statements:
(A) The figures meet the stated condition for being comparative data.
(B) Expressing each item as a percentage of a common item is the defining basis of a comparative statement.
(C) If different accounting principles are used in two periods, the deviation should be mentioned in a footnote.
(D) The comparison of figures for different periods is called vertical analysis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (D) only","(A) and (C) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Statement (A) is correct because the company used the same accounting principles in both periods, the stated condition for comparative financial data. Statement (C) correctly identifies the footnote disclosure required when accounting principles differ. Statement (B) describes common-size statements, and comparative analysis is known as horizontal analysis, not vertical analysis.

Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector. 4.4 Tools of Analysis of Financial Statements The most commonly used techniques of financial analysis are as follows: 1. Comparative Statements: These are the statements showing the profitability and financial position of a firm for different periods of time in a comparative form to give an idea about the position of two or more periods. It usually applies to the two important financial statements, namely, balance sheet and statement of profit and loss prepared in a comparative form. The financial data will be comparative only when same accounting principles are used in preparing these statements. If this is not the case, the deviation in the use of accounting principles should be mentioned as a footnote. Comparative figures indicate the trend and direction of financial position and operating results. This analysis is also known as ‘horizontal analysis’. 2. Common Size Statements: These are the statements which indicate the relationship of different items of a financial statement with a common item by expressing each item as a percentage of that common item. The percentage thus calculated can be easily compared with the results of corresponding percentages of the previous year or of some other firms, as the numbers are brought to common base. Such statements also allow an analyst to compare the operating and financing characteristics of two companies of different sizes in the same industry. Thus, common size statements are useful, both, in intra-firm comparisons over different years and also in making inter-firm comparisons for the same year or for several years. Under the fixed capital method, a partner first introduces additional capital and later receives a share of profit and makes drawings. Assume there are no other partner transactions and that, after the profit and drawings are recorded, the Partner’s Current Account has a credit balance. Arrange the following steps in the order for recording the transactions and presenting the year-end balances:
(A) Record the share of profit and drawings in the Partner’s Current Account.
(B) Record the additional capital in the Partner’s Capital Account.
(C) Confirm the credit balance of the Partner’s Current Account after its items are recorded.
(D) Show the Partner’s Capital Account and the credit-balance Current Account on the liabilities side of the balance sheet.
Choose the correct sequence.
explanation: Under the fixed capital method, additional capital is recorded in the Partner’s Capital Account, while the share of profit and drawings are recorded in the Partner’s Current Account. Since the additional capital is introduced first, B precedes A; the Current Account balance is confirmed after its items are recorded, and its stated credit balance is then shown on the liabilities side. The correct sequence is B–A–C–D.

body: A company’s inventory turnover ratio rose from 4 times to 8 times. During the period with the higher ratio, it bought inventory in small lots and sold goods quickly at low margins to realise cash. Both ratios are calculated on the same basis. Which conclusion is most defensible?
options: ["The increase establishes improved profitability, since every rise in inventory turnover necessarily reflects a better profit margin.","The increase indicates less frequent inventory conversion, since low-margin sales reduce the number of inventory turns.","The increase is a danger signal of obsolete inventory, since high turnover has the same significance as low turnover.","The increase is consistent with more frequent inventory conversion, but does not by itself establish improved profitability because quick low-margin sales may account for it."]
explanation: Inventory turnover reflects the frequency with which inventory is converted into revenue from operations. A high turnover ratio must be interpreted carefully because it may result from selling quickly at a low margin to realise cash; therefore, the increase alone does not establish improved profitability.

body: At the same reporting date, Company A has total assets of ₹2,00,00,000 and inventory of ₹20,00,000; Company B has total assets of ₹1,00,00,000 and inventory of ₹20,00,000. Assume each inventory amount is included in its company’s stated total assets. Using total assets as the common-size balance-sheet base, what percentage of total assets does inventory represent in each company?
options: ["Company A: 10%; Company B: 20%","Company A: 20%; Company B: 10%","Company A: 10%; Company B: 10%","Company A: 20%; Company B: 20%"]
explanation: A common-size balance sheet expresses each asset as a percentage of total assets. Company A’s inventory is ₹20,00,000 ÷ ₹2,00,00,000 = 10% of its total assets, while Company B’s inventory is ₹20,00,000 ÷ ₹1,00,00,000 = 20%.

For example, a common size balance sheet shows the percentage of each asset to the total assets, and that of each liability to the total liabilities. Common size analysis is of immense use for comparing enterprises which differ substantially in size as it provides an insight into the structure of financial statements. Assume the safety finding and the misleading nature of the planned claim are as stated. Which conclusion best applies the concept of consumer protection to this decision?

explanation: Consumer protection is intended to safeguard consumers’ interests and protect them from unethical business practices. The excerpt specifically identifies unsafe products and false or misleading advertising as such practices, so the firm’s proposed conduct fits the stated concern. Consider the following statements about the timing of measuring actual performance:
(A) It is generally believed that measurement should be done after the task is completed.
(B) Wherever possible, measurement of work should be done during performance.
(C) Even where measurement during performance is possible, measurement should be done only after the task is completed.
(D) Measurement should be done during performance for every task, whether or not such measurement is possible.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(A) and (B) only","(B) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: The guidance distinguishes the general belief that measurement is done after completion from the recommendation to measure during performance wherever possible. Therefore, statements (A) and (B) are correct. Statement (C) removes the stated exception, while (D) makes in-progress measurement unconditional.

body:
Match each management situation in List-I with the principle in List-II that it best illustrates.

List-I
(A) A company allows branch managers to decide routine local matters, while the head office retains final authority.
(B) A manager refuses to misuse her powers for a family benefit at the cost of the company's general interest, thereby setting an example for workers.
(C) An employee communicates with a colleague in another department by following the formal authority route through the intervening levels.
(D) A company fixes employees' wages at a level that provides a reasonable standard of living and remains within the company's paying capacity.

List-II
(I) Scalar Chain
(II) Centralisation and Decentralisation
(III) Remuneration of Employees
(IV) Subordination of Individual Interest to General Interest

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Branch managers deciding routine matters while the head office retains final authority illustrates the balance between decentralisation and centralisation. The manager's choice places general interest ahead of individual benefit; the formal communication route illustrates scalar chain; and the wage decision reflects fair remuneration within the company's paying capacity. Therefore, the correct mapping is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I) and (D)-(III).

body:
During a review of a country with stable political conditions, an analyst uses this causal model: confidence among business people supports investment in long-term projects to create new businesses, and the creation of new businesses contributes to growth of the economy. Arrange the listed developments from the first consequence of political stability to the broadest outcome.

(A) Creation of new businesses
(B) Confidence among business people to invest
(C) Growth of the economy
(D) Investment in long-term projects to create new businesses

Choose the correct sequence.
explanation: Political stability first builds confidence among business people to invest. That confidence is followed by investment in long-term projects intended to create new businesses, and the creation of new businesses is linked to growth of the economy. Thus, the sequence is (B), (D), (A), (C).

body: A wholesaler keeps its posted unit price unchanged but deliberately holds back part of its stock from distribution, thereby reducing the flow of supplies. Consumers consequently pay an additional amount elsewhere for the same goods; the case stipulates that this additional cost is unjustified. The goods have no fault or inadequacy in quality, nature or performance, and no fault or omission in any service is involved. Which concept best classifies the wholesaler’s conduct?
options: ["A defect in the goods","A deficiency in the service","A restrictive trade practice","Product liability"]
explanation: The unchanged posted price does not rule out a restrictive trade practice: the wholesaler’s action affects the flow of supplies and results in an unjustified cost to consumers. The stated facts therefore fit the definition of a restrictive trade practice. The stem rules out a fault in the goods or a deficiency in service, so those classifications do not fit.

body: A manager finds that output in a critical area has fallen significantly beyond its permissible limit. The cause has not yet been established. Which response should guide the manager’s next step?
options: ["Treat an unrealistic standard as the cause without examining other possibilities.","Treat a defective process as the cause without examining other possibilities.","Treat inadequate resources as the cause without examining other possibilities.","Analyse possible causes before attributing the deviation to any one explanation."]
explanation: The deviation is significant and beyond its permissible limit, so its causes should be analysed. A deviation may have more than one possible cause, including standards, processes, resources, organisational constraints or environmental factors. Therefore, selecting one cause before examining the possibilities is not justified.

Match each organisational arrangement in List-I with the corresponding Fayol principle in a contemporary (NOW) classification.
List-I
(A) Employees, rather than managers, are empowered.
(B) Subordinates report to multiple bosses.
(C) Functions have multiple plans and multiple bosses.
(D) Rewards are performance-based.
List-II
(I) Unity of Direction
(II) Remuneration of personnel
(III) Authority and Responsibility
(IV) Unity of Command
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The contemporary classification pairs employee empowerment with Authority and Responsibility, multiple-boss reporting with Unity of Command, multiple plans and bosses with Unity of Direction, and performance-based rewards with Remuneration of personnel. According to Fayol, discipline requires good superiors at all levels, clear and fair agreements and judicious application of penalties. Suppose management and labour union have entered into an agreement whereby workers have agreed to put in extra hours without any additional payment to revive the company out of loss. In return the management has promised to increase wages of the workers when this mission is accomplished. Here discipline when applied would mean that the workers and management both honour their commitments without any prejudice towards one another. (iv) Unity of Command: According to Fayol there should be one and only one boss for every individual employee. If an employee gets orders from two superiors at the same time the principle of unity of command is violated. The principle of unity of command states that each participant in a formal organisation should receive orders from and be responsible to only one superior. Fayol gave a lot of importance to this principle. He felt that if this principle is violated “authority is undermined, discipline is in jeopardy, order disturbed and stability threatened”. The principle resembles military organisation. Dual subordination should be avoided. This is to prevent confusion regarding tasks to be done. A new enterprise has completed planning and organising and has created its organisation structure. Arrange the following staffing activities in the order described:
(A) Recruitment
(B) Identification of the workforce requirement
(C) Placement
(D) Selection
Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: After the organisation structure is created, staffing first identifies the workforce requirement. The activities then proceed through recruitment, selection and placement, giving the sequence B-A-D-C.

body: A non-profit consumer organisation receives two requests. In case (i), one purchaser asks the organisation to lodge a consumer-court complaint on that purchaser’s behalf about a defective product. In case (ii), a residents’ group asks it to initiate a consumer-court case concerning an unfair seller practice affecting consumers generally; no individual is seeking the case on their behalf. Which pair correctly classifies the organisation’s role in (i) and (ii), respectively?
options: ["(i) Initiate a case in the general public interest; (ii) lodge a complaint on behalf of an individual consumer","(i) Provide legal assistance; (ii) initiate a case in the general public interest","(i) Lodge a complaint on behalf of an individual consumer; (ii) initiate a case in the general public interest","(i) Encourage consumers to protest; (ii) provide legal assistance"]
explanation: A consumer organisation may file a consumer-court complaint on behalf of an individual consumer. Separately, taking the initiative to file a case in a consumer court is identified as a role when the case is in the interest of the general public, not an individual. The two requests therefore match the roles in option C, respectively.

body: A self-service fast-food chain uses a waiting-time standard for customers. After an internal business change, management finds that the existing standard is no longer realistic. What should management do?
options: ["Modify the standard so that it is realistic in the changed business environment.","Keep the standard unchanged once it has been set.","Modify the standard after every internal change, even when it remains realistic.","Treat a modified standard as no longer serving as a benchmark."]
explanation: Standards are benchmarks and should be flexible enough to be modified when required. Since the internal change has made this standard unrealistic, management may modify it to make it realistic in the changed business environment.

body:
Match each coordination characteristic in List-I with the situation in List-II that best illustrates it.

List-I
(A) Coordination integrates group efforts
(B) Coordination ensures unity of action
(C) Coordination is a continuous process
(D) Coordination is an all-pervasive function

List-II
(I) Coordination is arranged at each management level because the activities of different departments are interdependent.
(II) Coordination starts during planning and continues through controlling, rather than being treated as a single event.
(III) Groups with diverse work interests are brought together into purposeful activity, with a common focus so that performance follows the plan and schedule.
(IV) Coordination binds departments so that all their actions are directed towards the organisation's common purpose.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Bringing groups with diverse work interests into purposeful activity with a common focus illustrates the integration of group efforts. Departments being bound to act towards a common purpose illustrates unity of action; coordination from planning through controlling is continuous, while coordination at every management level due to interdependent departmental activities is all-pervasive. The resulting mapping is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

body:
In a workplace, employees form social ties through interaction and use those ties to communicate about a proposal. Assume the communication uses an informal network rather than a planned route. Arrange the following events in a logically supported sequence, from the origin of the network to its communication outcome.
(A) Employees interact socially.
(B) A network of social relationships arises from their interaction.
(C) Communication takes place through a route that is not planned.
(D) Information spreads faster and feedback is quick.
explanation: Social interaction gives rise to the informal network, which can carry communication through an unplanned route. The communication advantage follows: information spreads faster and feedback is quick. The other sequences place communication before the network, the network before its stated origin, or the outcome before the communication.

Advantages: The informal organisation offers many benefits. Important among them are given below: (a) Prescribed lines of communication are not followed. Thus, the informal organisation leads to faster spread of information as well as quick feedback. (b) It helps to fulfill the social needs of the members and allows them to find like minded people. This enhances their job satisfaction since it gives them a sense of belongingness in the organisation. (c) It contributes towards fulfillment of organisational objectives by compensating for inadequacies in the formal organisation. For example, employees reactions towards plans and policies can be tested through the informal network.","url":"https://www.ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs105.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":null,"kind":"reference"},{"id":"ncert-lebs105","locator":"quality-v4-c8d4ce1fa39d","text":"The formal organisation can be better understood by a study of its features which are as follows: (a) It specifies the relationships among various job positions and the nature of their inter ­ relationship. This clarifies who has to report to whom. (b) It is a means to achieve the objectives specified in the plans, as it lays down rules and procedures essential for their achievement. (c) Efforts of various departments are coordinated, interlinked and integrated through the formal organisation. (d) It is deliberately designed by the top management to facilitate the smooth functioning of the organisation. (e) It places more emphasis on work to be performed than interpersonal relationships among the employees. Advantages: Formal organisation offers many advantages. Some of the important ones are: (a) It is easier to fix responsibility since mutual relationships are clearly defined. (b) There is no ambiguity in the role that each member has to play as duties are specified. This also helps in avoiding duplication of effort. (c) Unity of command is maintained through an established chain of command. (d) It leads to effective accomplish­ ment of goals by providing a framework for the operations to be performed and ensuring that each employee knows the r ole he has to play. (e) It provides stability to the organ­ isation. This is because behaviour of employees can be fairly pre­ dicted since there are specific rules to guide them.","url":"https://www.ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebs105.pdf","publisher":"NCERT","title":null,"kind":"reference"}]

body: A firm’s plan sets a monthly production standard of 1,000 units for each of two units. At month-end, Unit P has produced 990 units and Unit Q has produced 800 units. Which approach should the manager use when determining corrective action?
options: ["Ignore the size of each shortfall and prescribe the same action solely because both units are below standard.","Treat the difference between the units’ actual outputs as each unit’s deviation, without comparing output with its own standard.","Compare each unit’s output with its own standard and let the extent of its deviation inform the nature of corrective action.","Use the actual outputs alone to determine corrective action, without referring to the planned standards."]
explanation: Unit P is 10 units below its standard, while Unit Q is 200 units below its standard. Planning provides the basis of control, and the nature of corrective action depends on the extent of deviation from the standard. Therefore, each unit’s output should be compared with its own standard; the question does not specify the particular corrective actions.

(ii) Planning is a primary function of management: Planning lays down the base for other functions of management. All other managerial functions are performed within the framework of the plans drawn. body: A packing unit wants to reduce both packing time and wrapping-material waste. The manager can trial two proposed arrangements of the packing steps. The arrangements can be tested on comparable batches using the same workers, tools and input quantities; elapsed time and wrapping material used can be recorded. Which action best applies a scientific approach to deciding between the arrangements?
options: ["Use the arrangement favoured by experienced packers, then standardise it after observing routine work, without comparing the two proposed arrangements through a measured trial.","Choose the arrangement supervisors predict will be fastest, estimate material use, and standardise it without testing both arrangements under comparable conditions.","Test both arrangements on comparable batches with the same workers, tools and inputs, record time and waste, then standardise the method indicated by the results.","Let each shift retain its customary arrangement, then standardise whichever appears smoothest from the manager’s informal inspection, without recording comparative results."]
explanation: Testing both arrangements under comparable conditions and recording time and material use applies scientific inquiry to the stated alternatives. Standardising the method indicated by those results follows the principle of developing a standard method through study and analysis.

At a small organisation, the line manager is reviewing two career moves: Employee P would receive a new title but no increase in responsibility; Employee Q would be placed in a position of increased responsibility. Consider the following statements about promotions and employee development:
(A) Placing an employee in a position of increased responsibility is a promotion.
(B) A title change without an increase in responsibility is a promotion.
(C) Promotions are an integral part of a person’s career.
(D) The manager should encourage employees to grow and realise their full potential.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (C) and (D) only","(A), (B) and (C) only","(A), (B) and (D) only","(B), (C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Statements (A), (C) and (D) are correct: promotion means placement in a position of increased responsibility, promotions are an integral part of a person’s career, and the manager should encourage employees to grow and realise their potential. Employee P’s title change alone does not meet the stated meaning of promotion because responsibility does not increase. Therefore, option A is correct.

Match List-I with List-II on the stated business-environment changes and their implications.

List-I
(A) Increase in life expectancy and awareness for health care
(B) New health products and services
(C) Technological improvements
(D) Changes in fashions and tastes of consumers

List-II
(I) May render existing products obsolete
(II) May shift demand from existing products to new ones
(III) May increase demand for health products and services
(IV) Have, in turn, changed people’s lifestyles

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: The increase in life expectancy and health-care awareness is linked to increased demand for health products and services. New health products and services have, in turn, changed people’s lifestyles. The excerpt also links technological improvements with possible product obsolescence and changes in consumer tastes with shifts in demand.

body:
A consumer association finds widespread ignorance about consumers’ rights and available reliefs. It plans an educational initiative specifically to achieve consumer awareness. Arrange the following stages in the logical order from problem identification to intended outcome.
(A) Consumers attain awareness of their rights and available reliefs.
(B) Widespread ignorance of consumers about their rights and available reliefs is identified.
(C) Consumers are educated about those rights and reliefs.
explanation: The stated need is to address consumers’ ignorance about their rights and available reliefs through education. That education is intended to achieve consumer awareness. Therefore, the logical order is to identify the ignorance, educate consumers, and then attain awareness.

body: A firm is planning production of one product. Four managers are involved in preparing one common plan, and each has proposed a different forecast of the product’s future demand. No forecast is stated to be more accurate than the others. What should the managers do to use these forecasts as planning premises?
options: ["Let each manager use the demand forecast preferred by that manager.","Let the senior manager choose a forecast without agreement from the other managers.","Agree on one demand forecast and ensure that all four managers know and use it.","Use each forecast in a separate part of the common plan and reconcile them after production begins."]
explanation: Planning premises are assumptions on which plans are drawn, and they must be the same for all with total agreement. All managers involved in planning should be familiar with and use those same assumptions, so the managers should agree on one demand forecast and use it in the common plan.

body:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) A firm has a larger number of warehouses serving customers at different locations.
(B) An agricultural product requires long-term storage.
(C) A product, such as machinery, is bulky and difficult to ship.
(D) A product, such as bakery goods, is perishable.

List-II
(I) A larger warehouse count is generally associated with less time to serve customers at different locations and greater warehousing cost.
(II) Warehouses are located near production sites to help minimise charges on transporting the goods.
(III) Warehouses are placed at different locations near the market in view of bulk and shipping difficulty.
(IV) Warehouses are placed at different locations near the market for a perishable product.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A larger number of warehouses is generally associated with less time to serve customers at different locations but greater warehousing cost, so (A) matches (I). Long-term storage of agricultural products is associated with warehouses near production sites to help minimise transportation charges, so (B) matches (II). Bulky, hard-to-ship products and perishable products are both kept at different locations near the market, matching (C) with (III) and (D) with (IV).

Inventory Control: Linked to warehousing decisions are the inventory decisions which hold key to success for many manufacturers, especially those where the per unit cost is high. A very important decision in respect of inventory is deciding about the level of inventory. Higher the level of inventory, higher will be the level of service to customers but the cost of carrying the inventory will also be high because lot of capital would be tied up in the stock. Thus, a balance is to be maintained in respect of the cost and customer satisfaction. body: A management and a labour union agree that workers will put in extra hours without additional payment to help revive a company from loss. Management promises to increase the workers’ wages when the mission is accomplished. The workers complete the extra hours, the mission is accomplished, and both parties honour their commitments. Which principle of management is illustrated?
options: ["Discipline","Unity of Command","Unity of Direction","Remuneration of Personnel"]
explanation: Discipline involves obedience to organisational rules and employment agreements. Here, both the workers and management honour the commitments they made.

According to Fayol, discipline requires good superiors at all levels, clear and fair agreements and judicious application of penalties. Suppose management and labour union have entered into an agreement whereby workers have agreed to put in extra hours without any additional payment to revive the company out of loss. In return the management has promised to increase wages of the workers when this mission is accomplished. Here discipline when applied would mean that the workers and management both honour their commitments without any prejudice towards one another. (iv) Unity of Command: According to Fayol there should be one and only one boss for every individual employee. If an employee gets orders from two superiors at the same time the principle of unity of command is violated. The principle of unity of command states that each participant in a formal organisation should receive orders from and be responsible to only one superior. Fayol gave a lot of importance to this principle. He felt that if this principle is violated “authority is undermined, discipline is in jeopardy, order disturbed and stability threatened”. The principle resembles military organisation. Dual subordination should be avoided. This is to prevent confusion regarding tasks to be done. Suppose a sales person is asked to clinch a deal with a buyer and is allowed to give 10% discount by the marketing manager. But finance department tells her/ him not to offer more than 5% discount. Now there is no unity of command. This can be avoided if there is coordination between various departments. (v) Unity of Direction: All the units of an organisation should be moving towards the same objectives through coordinated and focussed efforts. explanation: D follows because major common economic activities in a region affect overall human development in a shared environment. The stated rationale is the shared economic and human-development context, not an assumption of political similarity. The excerpt specifically notes little similarity between the political power setups of India, Pakistan and China.

An economy records the following changes:
Year 1 to Year 2: GDP index rises from 200 to 220; employed persons increase from 80 million to 84 million.
Year 2 to Year 3: GDP index rises from 220 to 242; employed persons remain at 84 million.
Calculate percentage changes using (final value − initial value) ÷ initial value × 100. For this question, an increase in the GDP index represents an increase in production of goods and services, and jobless growth means an increase in production without generating employment. Which statement is correct?
options: ["GDP grew by 10% in each interval; employment grew by 5% and then 0%, so Year 2 to Year 3 shows jobless growth.","GDP grew by 10% in each interval; employment grew by 5% in each interval, so neither interval shows jobless growth.","GDP grew by 10% in each interval; employment grew by 5% and then 0%, so Year 1 to Year 2 shows jobless growth.","GDP grew by 10% and 9.09% in the two intervals; employment grew by 5% and then 0%, so Year 2 to Year 3 shows jobless growth."]
explanation: From Year 1 to Year 2, GDP growth is (220 − 200) ÷ 200 × 100 = 10%, and employment growth is (84 − 80) ÷ 80 × 100 = 5%. From Year 2 to Year 3, GDP growth is (242 − 220) ÷ 220 × 100 = 10%, while employment growth is 0%. Thus, production increases without generating employment in the second interval, which meets the stated meaning of jobless growth.

Match each practice in List-I with the sustainability requirement in List-II. The fish stock in (A) is renewable, and the resource in (B) is non-renewable. All rates refer to the same time interval.
List-I
(A) A fish stock is harvested at a rate equal to its rate of regeneration.
(B) A non-renewable resource is depleted at a rate no greater than the rate at which renewable substitutes are created.
(C) A production method supplies the same output using fewer inputs.
(D) Inefficiencies arising from pollution are corrected.
List-II
(I) Correct pollution-related inefficiencies.
(II) Make technological progress input-efficient rather than input-consuming.
(III) Limit non-renewable resource depletion by the creation of renewable substitutes.
(IV) Limit renewable-resource extraction by its rate of regeneration.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A matches IV because renewable-resource extraction should not exceed the rate of regeneration. B matches III because depletion of non-renewable resources should not exceed the rate at which renewable substitutes are created. C illustrates input-efficient technological progress, while D matches the requirement to correct inefficiencies arising from pollution.

(A) Enhanced human capital can raise labour productivity and stimulate innovation.
(B) An educated workforce can facilitate adaptation to new technologies.
(C) Human capital can raise labour productivity but cannot stimulate innovation.
(D) An educated workforce cannot facilitate adaptation to new technologies.

body:
In an economy, equilibrium output is below the full-employment level. Arrange the following statements in the logical order from this condition to its long-run price implication.

(A) The situation is termed deficient demand.
(B) Prices decline in the long run.
(C) Demand is insufficient to employ all factors of production.
(D) Equilibrium output is below the full-employment level.

Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: When equilibrium output is below the full-employment level, demand is insufficient to employ all factors of production. This situation is termed deficient demand, and prices decline in the long run. Thus, the logical order is (D)-(C)-(A)-(B).

body: A policy team has two objectives for imported products. For product X, it wants to set a maximum quantity that may be imported. For product Y, it wants imported goods to become more expensive so their use is discouraged. Domestic firms producing both products face competition from foreign firms. Which recommendation correctly matches the instruments to these objectives and states their common implication?
options: ["Use a tariff for X and a quota for Y; the tariff caps import quantity, while the quota makes imports more expensive; both restrict imports and protect domestic firms from foreign competition.","Use a quota for X and a tariff for Y; the quota caps import quantity and the tariff makes imports more expensive, but only the quota restricts imports and protects domestic firms from foreign competition.","Use a quota for X and a tariff for Y; the quota makes imports more expensive, while the tariff caps import quantity; both restrict imports and protect domestic firms from foreign competition.","Use a quota for X and a tariff for Y; the quota caps import quantity, while the tariff makes imports more expensive and discourages their use; both restrict imports and protect domestic firms from foreign competition."]
explanation: A quota specifies the quantity of goods that can be imported, so it fits the objective for product X. A tariff makes imported goods more expensive and discourages their use, so it fits the objective for product Y. Both tariffs and quotas restrict imports and thereby protect domestic firms from foreign competition, making D the only option that matches both objectives and the common implication.

body: A consumer’s optimal quantity demanded for a good is 10 units when its price is ₹20. The price rises to ₹25, while income, preferences and all other relevant conditions remain unchanged. What is the likely outcome for the quantity demanded?
options: ["It is likely to rise above 10 units.","It is likely to fall below 10 units.","It is likely to remain at 10 units.","It is likely to fall by exactly 5 units."]
explanation: With other relevant conditions unchanged, a rise in price is generally likely to reduce the consumer’s optimally chosen quantity. The stated relationship establishes the likely direction, not an exact numerical change.

body: In an economy, real GDP remains unchanged while the general price level index rises from 100 to 110. Assume no other relevant conditions change. Which conclusion about transaction demand for money is warranted?
options: ["It rises by exactly 10%.","It rises, but the percentage increase cannot be determined from the information given.","It remains unchanged because real GDP has not changed.","It falls because the general price level has risen."]
explanation: Transaction demand for money is positively related to the general price level as well as to real GDP. With real GDP unchanged and the price level higher, transaction demand rises. The stated relationship does not specify a formula that would establish an exact percentage increase.

body:
A review considers four issues in organic farming. Match each issue in List-I with the corresponding implication in List-II.

List-I
(A) Comparing organic yields with yields from modern agricultural farming during the initial years
(B) A small or marginal farmer considering adaptation to large-scale organic production
(C) Comparing organic produce with sprayed produce for blemishes and shelf life
(D) Planning the range of off-season crops under organic farming

List-II
(I) The choice of off-season crops is quite limited.
(II) Organic produce may have more blemishes and a shorter shelf life.
(III) Organic yields are lower during the initial years than yields from modern agricultural farming.
(IV) Small and marginal farmers may find adaptation to large-scale production difficult.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

A. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
B. (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
C. (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
D. (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
explanation: The initial-years yield comparison maps (A) to (III), and the scale-adaptation concern for small and marginal farmers maps (B) to (IV). The comparison with sprayed produce maps (C) to (II), while the limited choice of off-season crops maps (D) to (I). Therefore, option A gives the complete match.

(A) Pakistan was identified as having the highest outflow, with India next.
(B) The outflow was described as helping stimulate economic growth.
(C) India was identified as having the highest outflow, with Pakistan next.
(D) The outflow was described as impeding economic growth.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(A) and (D) only","(A) and (B) only"]
explanation: The note identifies Pakistan first and India second in the outflow, and states that the outflow helped stimulate economic growth. Statements (A) and (B) reflect these claims; (C) reverses the order, while (D) reverses the stated effect.

body:
A government-owned enterprise increases its output of goods and services. The private enterprises considered here receive raw materials from it. Arrange these events from the initiating event to the final effect.

(A) Employment opportunities in the economy increase.
(B) Output rises in the private enterprises receiving the raw materials.
(C) Output of goods and services from the government-owned enterprise increases.

Choose the correct sequence:
explanation: The increase in output by the government-owned enterprise is the initiating event. Private enterprises receiving its raw materials then raise their output, and the resulting increase in employment opportunities is the final effect. The sequence is (C)-(B)-(A).

body: In a period of high employment, aggregate demand is ₹9,60,000 crore and available output is ₹8,40,000 crore. A restrictive measure has already reduced aggregate demand by ₹30,000 crore. Assume that the measure reduces demand rupee for rupee, available output remains unchanged, and the government’s target is to reduce aggregate demand to available output. What additional reduction in aggregate demand is required?
explanation: The initial excess of aggregate demand over available output is ₹1,20,000 crore. After the ₹30,000 crore reduction already made, the remaining excess is ₹90,000 crore, which is the additional reduction required. Reducing demand is the appropriate stabilising response when demand exceeds available output under conditions of high employment.

body:
A producer adds a newly produced machine to its physical capital. It uses raw materials in production and retains some finished goods that have been produced but not sold. Consider the following statements:
(A) The newly produced machine added to physical capital is included in investment.
(B) The raw materials used in production are investment goods.
(C) The finished goods produced but not sold and retained by the producer form inventory.
(D) A machine produced during the year is used up in producing other goods during that year.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A) and (B) only","(A) and (C) only","(B) and (D) only","(C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Investment includes additions to physical capital and changes in the producer’s finished-goods inventory, so (A) and (C) are correct. Raw materials are intermediate goods, not investment goods, and machines produced during a year are not used up in producing other goods.

Note that ‘investment goods’ (such as machines) are also part of the final goods – they are not intermediate goods like raw materials. Machines produced in an economy in a given year are not ‘used up’ to produce other goods but yield their services over a number of years. Investment decisions by producers, such as whether to buy a new machine, depend, to a large extent, on the market rate of interest. However, for simplicity, we assume here that firms plan to invest the same amount every year. AD = C + I. Substituting the values of C and I from equations (4.1) and (4.2), aggregate demand for final goods can be written as AD = C + I + c.Y If the final goods market is in equilibrium this can be written as Y = C + I + c.Y where Y is the ex ante, or planned, ouput of final goods. This equation can be further simplified by adding up the two autonomous terms, C and I , making it Y = A + c.Y (4.3) where A = C + I is the total autonomous expenditure in the economy. In reality, these two components of autonomous expenditure behave in different ways. C , representing subsistence consumption level of an economy, remains more or less stable over time. However, I has been observed to undergo periodic fluctuations. A word of caution is in order. The term Y on the left hand side of equation (4.3) represents the ex ante output or the planned supply of final goods. On the other hand, the expression on the right hand side denotes ex ante or planned aggregate demand for final goods in the economy. Ex ante supply is equal to ex ante demand only when the final goods market, and hence the economy, is in equilibrium. Equation (4.3) should not, therefore, be confused with the accounting identity of Chapter 2, which states that the ex post value of total output must always be equal to the sum total of ex post consumption and ex post investment in the economy. If ex ante demand for final goods falls short of the output of final goods that the producers have planned to produce in a given year, equation (4.3) will not hold. Stocks will be piling up in the warehouses which we may consider as unintended accumulation of inventories . It should be noted that inventories or stocks refers to that part of output produced which is not sold and therefore remains with the firm. Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
(A) India became self-sufficient in food-grain production thanks to the Green Revolution.
(B) Land reforms and promotion of HYV seeds were used to address agricultural issues.
(C) During colonial rule, the agricultural sector had neither growth nor equity.
(D) Promotion of HYV seeds ushered in a revolution in Indian agriculture.
Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:
explanation: The agricultural condition during colonial rule came before the measures taken by independent India to address the issues. Promotion of HYV seeds ushered in a revolution in Indian agriculture, and India became self-sufficient in food-grain production thanks to the Green Revolution.

body: A case file on an economy under colonial rule records a total population of 2,00,000. It classifies 1,04,000 people as deriving their livelihood directly from agriculture and 66,000 as deriving it indirectly. These groups are mutually exclusive and together comprise the 1,70,000 residents who live mostly in villages. The remaining 30,000 derive their livelihood neither directly nor indirectly from agriculture. Which calculation correctly gives the agriculture-linked share of the population and matches the stated profile?
options: ["Combine the direct and indirect groups: 1,70,000 out of 2,00,000, or 85%.","Count only the direct group: 1,04,000 out of 2,00,000, or 52%.","Combine the direct group and the group with neither link: 1,34,000 out of 2,00,000, or 67%.","Count only the indirect group: 66,000 out of 2,00,000, or 33%."]
explanation: The directly and indirectly agriculture-linked groups are mutually exclusive, so their total is 1,04,000 + 66,000 = 1,70,000. Dividing by the total population of 2,00,000 gives 85%, matching the stated profile. The remaining 30,000 are explicitly described as having neither link, so they are not included.

body: Let x1 denote the quantity of bananas and x2 the quantity of mangoes. A consumer spends the entire fixed budget on these two goods. Their positive prices remain unchanged, and the price of one banana is greater than the price of one mango. If the consumer moves between bundles on the same budget line and increases the quantity of bananas, which statement describes the trade-off?
options: ["More than one mango is given up for each additional banana.","Less than one mango is given up for each additional banana.","Exactly one mango is given up for each additional banana.","Mangoes increase as bananas increase along the budget line."]
explanation: The slope of the budget line is ∆x2/∆x1 = −p1/p2. Since the price of a banana is greater than the price of a mango, p1/p2 is greater than 1, so more than one mango is given up for each additional banana along the budget line. The slope is negative, so mangoes do not increase as bananas increase.

In general, demand for a necessity is likely to be price inelastic while demand for a luxury good is likely to be price elastic. For each ₹5 increase in price from ₹20, quantity demanded falls by 10 units and quantity supplied rises by 10 units. These changes continue over the price range needed to reach equilibrium, with no other changes. What are the equilibrium price and quantity?

body:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) RBI buys a Government bond in the open market and pays by cheque.
(B) RBI sells a Government bond to private individuals or institutions.
(C) In the banking-system example, the reserve ratio is increased from 20 per cent to 25 per cent.
(D) The Central bank uses moral suasion to persuade commercial banks to discourage lending.

List-II
(I) Reserves and money supply increase.
(II) Reserves and money supply decrease.
(III) Banks must call back some loans to meet the higher reserve requirement, and money supply falls.
(IV) Lending is influenced through persuasion, a qualitative tool.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
(A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
(A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
(A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
explanation: When the RBI buys a Government bond and pays by cheque, reserves and money supply increase; when it sells a bond, both decrease. In the stated banking-system example, increasing the reserve ratio from 20 per cent to 25 per cent requires banks to call back some loans, so money supply falls. Moral suasion uses persuasion to influence lending and is a qualitative tool.

For one period, an economy has GVA at factor cost of ₹8,00,000. It pays production taxes of ₹70,000 and product taxes of ₹50,000, and receives production subsidies of ₹10,000 and product subsidies of ₹20,000. These are the only production taxes, product taxes and subsidies for the period.

Consider the following statements:
(A) Net production taxes are ₹60,000.
(B) GVA at basic prices is ₹8,60,000.
(C) Net product taxes are ₹30,000.
(D) GDP at market prices is ₹8,80,000.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: ["(A), (B) and (D) only","(A), (B) and (C) only","(A), (C) and (D) only","(B), (C) and (D) only"]
explanation: Net production taxes are ₹70,000 − ₹10,000 = ₹60,000, so GVA at basic prices is ₹8,00,000 + ₹60,000 = ₹8,60,000. Net product taxes are ₹50,000 − ₹20,000 = ₹30,000, so GDP at market prices is ₹8,60,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹8,90,000. Thus statements (A), (B) and (C) are correct, while (D) is not.

In its revision in January 2015 the CSO replaced GDP at factor cost with the GVA at basic prices, and the GDP at market prices, which is now called only GDP, is now the most highlighted measure. The idea of GVA has already been discussed: it is the value of total output produced in the economy less the value of intermediate consumption (the output which is used in production of output further, and not used in final consumption). Here we discuss the concept of basic prices. The distinction between factor cost, basic prices and market prices is based on the distinction between net production taxes (production taxes less production subsidies) and net product taxes (product taxes less product subsidies). Production taxes and subsidies are paid or received in relation to production and are independent of the volume of production such as land revenues, stamp and registration fee. Product taxes and subsidies, on the other hand, are paid or received per unit or product, e.g., excise tax, service tax, export and import duties etc. Factor cost includes only the payment to factors of production, it does not include any tax. In order to arrive at the market prices, we have to add to the factor cost the total indirect taxes less total subsidies. The basic prices lie in between: they include the production taxes (less production subsidies) but not product taxes (less product subsidies). Therefore in order to arrive at market prices we have to add product taxes (less product subsidies) to the basic prices. As stated above, now the CSO releases GVA at basic prices. Arrange the following steps in the order in which a rural SHG’s member-savings and credit cycle occurs.
(A) Credit from the pooled money is given to a needy member.
(B) The credit is repaid in small instalments at reasonable interest.
(C) Each member makes a minimum thrift contribution.
(D) The contributions are pooled.
Choose the correct sequence.
explanation: Members’ thrift contributions form the pool, and credit is given to needy members from that pool. Repayment follows the credit and is made in small instalments at reasonable interest, so the sequence is (C)-(D)-(A)-(B).

body:
A farm keeps its land fixed at 4 hectares and changes only the number of workers. The observed total output is:
Workers employed: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
Total output (units): 0, 10, 24, 42, 56, 66, 72
Assuming the observations are comparable, which interpretation is supported?
options: ["Total product falls from the fourth worker onward because each added worker contributes less.","Marginal product rises through the fourth worker and falls only from the fifth worker onward.","Marginal product begins to fall with the fourth worker, although total product continues to rise.","Marginal product does not fall because total output increases with every additional worker."]
explanation: The successive additions to output are 10, 14, 18, 14, 10 and 6 units. Thus, the marginal product rises through the third worker and falls with the fourth worker, while total output still rises from 42 to 56 units and thereafter. A fall in marginal product does not mean that total product has begun to fall.

Initially, as we increase the amount of the variable input, the factor proportions become more and more suitable for the production and marginal product increases. Suppose table 3.2 describes the output of a farmer who has 4 hectares of land, and can choose how much labour he wants to use. If he uses only 1 worker, he has too much land for the worker to cultivate alone. As he increases the number of workers, the amount of labour per unit land increases, and each worker adds proportionally more and more to the total output. Marginal product increases in this phase. When the fourth worker is hired, the land begins to get ‘crowded’. Each worker now has insufficient land to work efficiently. So the output added by each additional worker is now proportionally less. body: In a market with many buyers and sellers, all sellers offer the same homogeneous product, and buyers have perfect information about its market price of ₹20 per unit. Assume buyers are price takers. A buyer who wants several units first offers ₹18 per unit and then considers offering ₹20 per unit. Which outcome should she expect?
options: ["At ₹18, no seller will sell to her; at ₹20, she can buy only a fixed quantity.","At ₹18, some sellers may sell to her; at ₹20, she can buy as many units as she desires.","At ₹18, no seller will sell to her; she must offer more than ₹20 to obtain any units.","At ₹18, no seller will sell to her; at ₹20, she can obtain as many units as she desires."]
explanation: A price-taking buyer believes that no firm will sell to her at a price below the market price. At ₹20, which equals the market price, she can obtain as many units as she desires, so D is correct.

Perfect information implies that all buyers and all sellers are completely informed about the price, quality and other relevant details about the product, as well as the market. These features result in the single most distinguishing characteristic of perfect competition: price taking behaviour. From the viewpoint of a firm, what does price-taking entail? A price-taking firm believes that if it sets a price above the market price, it will be unable to sell any quantity of the good that it produces. On the other hand, should the set price be less than or equal to the market price, the firm can sell as many units of the good as it wants to sell. From the viewpoint of a buyer, what does price-taking entail? A buyer would obviously like to buy the good at the lowest possible price. However, a price-taking buyer believes that if she asks for a price below the market price, no firm will be willing to sell to her. On the other hand, should the price asked be greater than or equal to the market price, the buyer can obtain as many units of the good as she desires to buy. Price-taking is often thought to be a reasonable assumption when the market has many firms and buyers have perfect information about the price prevailing in the market. Why? Let us start with a situation where each firm in the market charges the same (market) price. Suppose, now, that a certain firm raises its price above the market price. Observe that since all firms produce the same good and all buyers are aware of the market price, the firm in question loses all its buyers. Furthermore, as these buyers switch their purchases to other firms, no “adjustment” problems arise; their demand is readily accommodated when there are so many other firms in the market.
